subject: TideCommerce: throughput surge & RCA with remediation commitments
messages:
From: Alec Hart <alec.hart@tidecommerce.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@cloudinfra.io>, ops@tidecommerce.com
Date: 2026-09-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 5xxs and token latency – urgent

David —

We had a major customer-facing incident this morning between 07:40–08:05 PT where API error rate jumped to ~14% and P95 generation latency doubled (from ~220ms to ~480ms). This affected checkout flows for multiple merchants. Our engineering team saw many 5xx responses from the Redwood generation endpoint and sustained queueing on our side.

Can you confirm you’re aware and share immediate mitigation steps? We’re trying to decide whether to fail open to another provider or throttle traffic.

Impact: business-critical (payment flows blocked for ~25 min). We need an RCA and remediation timeline — cc’ing our SRE (Sofia).

Thanks,
Alec Hart
Head of Platform, TideCommerce

Attachments: tide-impact-summary-09152026.pdf
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Hart <alec.hart@tidecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:19:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xxs and token latency – urgent

Alec —

Thanks for the heads-up and sorry for the impact. We saw the same signal in our monitoring and immediately opened an incident bridge. Short summary of immediate actions taken:

- Scaled up inference pools for Tide traffic where possible.
- Rolled traffic to a fallback model variant (reduced context window) for critical routes to restore success rate.
- Temporarily increased request retry window in the gateway.

I’ll own the RCA and will share findings by EOD today. Marissa, Jonas — looping you in for customer communications and follow-through.

Short-term ask for Tide: please save any request IDs you can (sampled IDs are most useful). I’ve requested traces from our runtime and will attach interim notes.

David Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

If you want to add anything, reply-all and I’ll update the invite.

—Marissa

Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Alec Hart <alec.hart@tidecommerce.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: TideCommerce RCA: root causes and corrective actions (interim)

Folks —

Attached is the interim RCA (see tide-rca-20260915.pdf). High-level findings from initial investigation:

Root causes (short):
1) Serving runtime regression: a change in kernel selection logic (merged 2026-09-14) caused pathological KV-cache miss patterns for ~20% of requests (mostly long-conversation flows). This increased per-token CPU on the GPU host and raised service queuing.
2) Autoscale policy gap: our load classifier did not tag a subset of Tide traffic that had custom routing headers; autoscaler therefore under-provisioned during the spike.
3) Fallback model variant mismatch: the fallback model we routed to had a larger decoding loop due to mismatched prompt-format handling, resulting in longer latencies for some paths.

Immediate corrective actions (completed or in-progress):
- Reverted the kernel-selection change (completed 2026-09-15 13:12 PT).
- Manually expanded Tide’s dedicated pool by +30% capacity (completed during incident).
- Applied a hotfix to autoscale classifier to honor customer routing headers (deployed 2026-09-15 15:00 PT).
- Small prompt normalization fix to the fallback variant to match production prompts (deployed 2026-09-15 16:10 PT).

Planned follow-up commitments (owners & ETA):
- Deep performance regression test to prevent kernel selection regressions (owner: Jonas Weber) — ETA 2026-09-22
- Autoscale policy e2e test and synthetic load for header-tagged flows (owner: Laura Bennett) — ETA 2026-09-21
- Postmortem writeup + public-facing timeline for Tide (owner: David Kim) — ETA 2026-09-17
- Credits discussion & customer remediation proposal (owner: Marissa Cole) — initial proposal by 2026-09-18

I’ve attached traces (kv-cache-trace-20260915.log) and a diff of the autoscale policy change (autoscale-policy.diff). We’ll publish a final RCA doc once regression tests complete.

David Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tide-rca-20260915.pdf, kv-cache-trace-20260915.log, autoscale-policy.diff
From: Alec Hart <alec.hart@tidecommerce.com>

Subject: Re: TideCommerce RCA: root causes and corrective actions (interim)

David / team —

Thanks for the quick investigation and the interim RCA. A couple of immediate asks from our side:

1) We need a short one-page timeline we can share with leadership (payment ops and our CEO). Can you produce that by EOD tomorrow?
2) We also want a proposal for service credit for the incident window and a short note on what will prevent recurrence.

Appreciate the clarity on causes — the kernel selection regression explanation aligns with our traces. Please cc me on the regression test plan and the synthetic load results once ready.

Regards,
Alec
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Alec —

We’ll deliver the one-page timeline and a draft credit proposal tomorrow morning. Quick notes on next steps and owners (so we’re aligned):

- Timeline one-pager (David) — due 2026-09-18 09:00 PT
- Credit proposal & customer remediation package (Marissa) — due 2026-09-18 09:00 PT

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
